wheel.lug_torque: ≈76 lb-ft (103 N·m) alloy · ≈116 lb-ft (157 N·m) steel
wheel.note: Lug nuts changed from conical to washer type in 1995, so match nuts to the wheel. Torque figures are Rough Trax's Australian data (it says to confirm with Toyota); US owners quote about 75 lb-ft for alloys from the 1995-on owner's manual.

max_tire.note: IH8MUD's safe answer. Owners also report 305/70R16 and 295/75R16 fitting, depending on wheel width and offset; 35s rub badly on a stock truck.
Christo Slee: 35s work on a 2-inch Old Man Emu lift but will probably rub at full flex unless you lower the bump stops. Re-gear (4.56/4.88/5.29) is advised over the stock 4.11s.

items.title: Reese Class II trailer hitch (aftermarket equipment)
items.summary: The receiver weld on Reese hitch part no. 06070 can break and let a trailer separate; the remedy was a replacement hitch. NHTSA's database shows no Toyota-issued vehicle recalls for 1991–97 US Land Cruisers.

timeline.change: 80 Series launched (shown at the October 1989 Tokyo Motor Show); full-time 4WD and all-coil suspension for North America and Europe

First US model year (FJ80): 3F-E 4.0 L carried over from the FJ62, A440F auto, front disc / rear drum brakes, semi-float rear axle, no ABS, airbags or factory lockers; center-diff lock switch standard

FZJ80 arrives: 4.5 L 24-valve 1FZ-FE, A442F auto, 16-inch wheels; ABS trucks get a full-floating rear axle with discs and a viscous-coupling transfer case; factory front and rear lockers become optional; center-diff switch dropped (wiring stays); A/C switches from R12 to R134a mid-year
Thicker front drive flanges from April 1994 build (43421-60040 replaces 43421-60022); last year of the TOYOTA-lettered grille
Redesigned dash with dual airbags, new Toyota oval logo, mass-air-flow emissions and voluntary OBD-II compatibility, A343F automatic (some '95s kept the A442F), washer-type lug nuts
Fully OBD-II; ABS and airbags standard; Lexus LX 450 twin launched; in-line catalytic converters
Final US year: 40th Anniversary Limited Edition (4,744 sold) and Collector's Edition; last year of the electric front locker; revised rear sway-bar brackets and aluminum radiator

identify.intro: Lockers, engine and build date change what an 80 is worth, and Lexus twins, re-badged imports and late Venezuelan builds muddy the water. Check the hardware, not the listing.

items.head: FJ80 vs FZJ80
items.body: 1991–92 FJ80s have the 4.0 L 3F-E pushrod six and 15-inch wheels; 1993–97 FZJ80s have the 4.5 L DOHC 1FZ-FE and 16-inch wheels. A center-diff lock switch on the dash is standard on 1991–92 trucks only.

items.head: Factory lockers
items.body: Optional 1993–97 (Toyota option code K294). Locked trucks have the front/rear locker rotary switch on the dash (switch 84725-60020). Test them: engage in low range on a loose surface and make sure the dash lights and the axle respond.

items.head: Transmission and build date
items.body: The transmission type (A442F or A343F on 1995 trucks) is printed on the label in the driver's door jamb. The A/C changed from R12 to R134a around VIN JT3DJ81xxxxx38947; R12 trucks have the dryer in front of the battery, R134a trucks behind the bumper.

items.head: Body-panel VIN stickers
items.body: Late 80s carry VIN stickers on most body panels. Missing stickers, overspray or filler on a panel point to accident repair.

items.head: Special editions and LX 450
items.body: The 1997 40th Anniversary has a serialized console badge, two-tone leather, black-chrome badges and sage or green paint. The LX 450 (1996–97) adds body cladding, softer suspension and a center-console subwoofer on the same FZJ80 running gear.

items.head: Chassis codes
items.body: Market codes add a suffix (for example FZJ80R); R means right-hand drive outside Japan. HDJ80 and HZJ80 diesels were never sold new in the US.

capability.note: KBB maximum for 1997; don't tow from the four holes in the rear crossmember, which aren't rated for towing in the US

values.intro: Clean 1993–97 FZJ80s with lockers have become collector trucks, while tired FJ80s and high-mile drivers are still cheap enough to wheel.
values.note: Based on 250 Bring a Trailer sales from January 2025 to October 2026 (median about $25,500). 1991–92 FJ80s sold for a median of about $15,750. 40th Anniversary and Collector's Edition trucks sold for a median of about $30,000, with the best near $90,000. An ICON-built 1995 FZJ80 made $124,500 and an imported HDJ80 turbodiesel $75,000.

docs.name: Toyota TIS (Technical Information System)
docs.note: Toyota's subscription service portal for most 1990-and-later North American models, including repair manuals, wiring diagrams and service bulletins.

paragraphs: The US only got gasoline 80s (the FJ80 and FZJ80). The HDJ80 turbodiesel and HZJ80 diesel, plus right-hand-drive and part-time-4WD trucks from Japan and Australia, are gray-market. NHTSA lets a vehicle be imported without meeting FMVSS once it is at least 25 years old, measured from its date of manufacture. Japanese 80 Series production ended in 1997, so every Japan-built 80 now qualifies.

Venezuela kept building 80s until 2007, so check the build date on any late Latin American truck. California is the hard state: Corsetti Cruisers warns that an import without a 50-state-compliant emissions system may be refused registration altogether. Check your state's DMV and emissions rules before you buy.

production.intro: Japanese production ran from 1990 to 1997, with Venezuelan assembly continuing to 2007. The US got the 1991–97 model years.

editions.name: 40th Anniversary Limited Edition
editions.note: 4,744 sold in the US: Antique Sage Pearl or Emerald Green, two-tone leather, serialized console badge, black-pearl badges; many were optioned with lockers

editions.name: Collector's Edition
editions.note: Badging, embroidered mats, automatic climate control, gray-windowed wheels and gray side moldings; available on many colors

community.name: Toyota Land Cruiser Association (TLCA)
community.note: US club since 1976 with regional chapters and the bimonthly Toyota Trails magazine; open to every Toyota 4x4 generation

community.name: Cruise Moab
community.note: TLCA's annual week of guided Land Cruiser trail runs in Moab, Utah, held each April

community.note: Salt Lake City museum with more than 100 Land Cruisers, aiming to show one of every model; open Monday–Saturday
